findings.reproduction: Run repro.py beside this verdict. It adapts the existing disposable real-TaskStore loader fixture: keep the registered task worktree pristine, change __init__.py only in the sibling caller repo, and call load(config,source_root=repo). Load succeeds, lifecycle.source reports clean=True for the registered worktree, but backend.source_package points at the modified sibling. counterexamples.json wrong_source_mount records both roots and differing contents. No Docker or actual FFF data is used.
findings.expected: Reject invocation from a different or dirty executable checkout, and bind the executing host package/task API and Docker-mounted worker package to the same inspected task worktree and qualified source. Source equality must be enforced before preparation or mutation.
findings.observed: TaskLifecycle fingerprints its registered worktree while DockerBackend mounts source_root from the caller. There is no equality/content check between those roots. Starting the CLI from a stale or dirty sibling checkout can therefore use a qualified task source/gate while running and mounting different, unreviewed code.

findings.reproduction: Run repro.py. On a fabricated 84-node archive, inject a sync-port failure immediately before archive-root directory fsync after the last rmdir. The first run leaves zero originals and an interrupted lifecycle. Recover with a sync spy. Recovery returns originals_retired=84 and marks complete with no archive-directory sync calls at all. See counterexamples.json unsynced_final_unlink. This is a call-order/fault-port proof, not a claim of an observed kernel crash.
findings.expected: Before acknowledging a recovered missing prefix or publishing terminal success, re-establish durability of the surviving parents affected by possibly unacknowledged unlink/rmdir effects, including the archive root when all84 originals are already absent. Preserve interruption on a failed reaffirmation.
findings.observed: prefix() treats every already-missing entry as retired, and retire() syncs parents only inside the remaining-entry loop. A failure between the final rmdir and its parent fsync leaves prefix84, so recovery skips every sync and publishes success. A subsequent crash may restore entries whose removal was never durably acknowledged, contradicting terminal accounting and the advertised unlink/sync recovery contract.

findings.reproduction: Run repro.py. Its fabricated artifact-root iterator yields10000 names, with a counter on enumeration. publish_manifest consumes all10000 before raising manifest-artifact-slots for its two-slot pool. See counterexamples.json unbounded_preparation_enumeration. The directory contains no actual retained data.
findings.expected: Use bounded streaming directory enumeration and refuse as soon as the two-slot publication precondition is exceeded, with finite allocations/work and a relevant deadline. Do not build a full list before checking its size.
findings.observed: list(root.iterdir()) materializes an arbitrarily large caller-selected directory before checking len(paths)<2. The read-only preparation path therefore has unbounded allocation/enumeration despite the declared two-slot pool and task requirement for complete bounded-allocation/I/O proofs.

findings.reproduction: Run raw-repro.py beside this verdict. It uses the actual tools.sandbox.bounded_capture with three fresh local Python subprocesses instead of Docker; each writes4000 synthetic stderr bytes and2 stdout bytes. All three DockerBackend.command calls succeed. raw-accounting-repro.json records12006 aggregate pipe bytes but backend.raw=6, and successively supplied limits8192,8190,8188.
findings.expected: Charge both captured stdout and stderr against one aggregate8192-byte operation allowance before admitting another transport command, including failures and recovery. Use a component-local adapter or an explicitly admitted transport contract change without weakening shared controls.
findings.observed: bounded_capture checks each command's combined pipes but returns stdout only. DockerBackend counts len(result.encode()), so successful stderr is dropped from aggregate accounting. Multiple commands exceed the operation raw-output cap while the public result reports a much smaller raw count. The counter is also only process-local and resets when a fresh recovery controller/backend is loaded.

findings.reproduction: Run python -B C:\Users\Huy\.codex\visualizations\2026\11\07\01a1b42a-4c36-7651-8c9d-165f5b27d818\m01-17-r2-architecture-security\reproduce.py from the isolated exact-head review worktree; inspect C:\Users\Huy\.codex\visualizations\2026\11\07\01a1b42a-4c36-7651-8c9d-165f5b27d818\m01-17-r2-architecture-security\counterexamples.json. All cases use fabricated disposable archives, fake Docker commands or a fresh temporary Git/TaskStore; no live FFF assets/resources are accessed. The terminal_after_deadline case advances the meter clock beyond its original deadline in the metadata-published fault port for the terminal record, representing terminal I/O completing after expiry.
findings.expected: Observe the original deadline after terminal publication and lifecycle finalization and refuse a successful return if it expired during those effects. Preserve an interrupted/uncertain disposition without a passing terminal receipt; apply the same rule to run and recover.
findings.observed: run returns success and marks the lifecycle complete even though meter.check immediately raises expired-or-sticky. There is no meter check after metadata.append(terminal) before success=True; recover repeats the same pattern at lines278-280. This contradicts the documented rule that late OS completion remains interrupted and cannot produce a passing terminal receipt.

enumeration_counterexample.stdlib_Path_iterdir:
def iterdir(self):
        """Yield path objects of the directory contents.

        The children are yielded in arbitrary order, and the
        special entries '.' and '..' are not included.
        """
        root_dir = str(self)
        with os.scandir(root_dir) as scandir_it:
            paths = [entry.path for entry in scandir_it]
        if root_dir == '.':
            paths = map(self._remove_leading_dot, paths)
        return map(self._from_parsed_string, paths)
